passage: I'm Lakshmi, and from the next balcony I watch Uday, who is two, open every drawer in his kitchen. He pulled out spoons, sniffed a steel bowl and put a fallen leaf in his mouth. His mother calmly took the leaf and said, "Leaf's not for eating." She moved the knives higher and put pots in the bottom drawer. Uday banged them, delighted. I can't know what he thinks, but he looked thrilled.

qa.q: What did Uday put in his mouth?
qa.a: Uday put a fallen leaf in his mouth.

qa.q: What was Uday probably feeling as he banged the pots?
qa.a: Uday seemed delighted and thrilled, though Lakshmi cannot know for certain what he was thinking.

qa.q: What did Uday's mother do that worked better than only saying no?
qa.a: She calmly took the leaf, moved the knives higher and put pots in the bottom drawer, so his exploring was safe and welcome.

qa.q: How might Uday's mother have felt watching him open every drawer?
qa.a: She probably felt watchful and a bit tired, but calm. She chose to make the kitchen safe instead of scolding.

grounding: A toddler opens drawers, mouths a leaf and pulls things around; safety-proofing works better than constant no, seen by a neighbour.

passage: Monday: Omkar, two, opened every drawer while his mother Ganga said "No, no" all day. Wednesday: Ganga locked the knife drawer and gave him the bottom one, filled with steel cups and wooden spoons. Saturday: Omkar dragged each thing out, tasted a spoon and banged a cup, and played for half an hour while Ganga cooked, no longer saying no.

qa.q: Which drawer did Ganga give Omkar?
qa.a: Ganga gave Omkar the bottom drawer, filled with steel cups and wooden spoons.

qa.q: What was Omkar feeling on Saturday as he banged the cup?
qa.a: Omkar was absorbed and happy, playing for half an hour on his own.

qa.q: What change made the difference between Monday and Saturday?
qa.a: Ganga locked the dangerous drawer and gave Omkar a safe one to explore, so the day stopped being a string of no's.

qa.q: How might Ganga have felt on Monday compared with Saturday?
qa.a: On Monday Ganga was probably worn out and anxious from saying no all day. On Saturday Ganga was calmer and able to cook.

grounding: A toddler opens drawers and tastes things; safety-proofing works better than constant saying no, shown across three days.
